_meta.use_case: Small-business tenant spaces: cafés and restaurants, bars, retail shops, salons, offices and fitness studios
_meta.code_basis: 2021 Seattle Building Code and related 2021 Seattle codes (2021 model codes with Washington State and Seattle amendments); Seattle Plumbing Code (Uniform Plumbing Code); 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; King County Board of Health Code and the Washington State Retail Food Code (chapter 246-215 WAC) for food businesses.
checked_against_city_sources: Code edition: SDCI's code adoption page lists the 2021 editions as adopted and the 2024 editions no sooner than May 2027.

Edition date (edition_date): the 2021 Seattle codes took effect on November 15, 2024. SDCI's 2021 Seattle Code Adoption page, https://www.glb.seattle.gov/sdci/codes/changes-to-code/2021-seattle-code-adoption: "The effective date for the 2021 Seattle codes was November 15, 2024." Confirmed by the owner, November 2026.

Occupant load factors (2021 SBC Table 1004.5); one exit up to 49 occupants for Groups A, B and M (Table 1006.2.1); 32 in. door clear width (1010.1.1); door swing at 50 occupants (1010.1.2.1); 0.2 in. of exit width per occupant (1005.3.2); exit signs not required where only one exit is required (1013.1 exception 1). Read from the 2021 Seattle Building Code Chapter 10 PDF.
Sprinkler triggers for Groups A-2, A-3 and M (903.2.1.2, 903.2.1.3, 903.2.7), read from the 2021 SBC Chapter 9 PDF.

Toilet and lavatory ratios for restaurants, bars, A-3, business and mercantile; the separate-facility exceptions (15, 25, 30 and 100 occupants); the struck-out service sink; the Uniform Plumbing Code. Read from the 2021 SBC Chapter 29 PDF. The business and mercantile rows were partly garbled in the extract, so re-check those two.
The 100-person Fire Department assembly permit, the permit list and the agencies: Seattle Office of Economic Development food business handbook and tenant improvement checklist.
Group B under 50 occupants: stated in a real SDCI Ordinance-review correction comment.

Zoning layer URL and field names: read from the live layer. Ground-floor shops and restaurants up to 2,500 sq ft in Neighborhood Residential zones: Ordinance 127376, SMC 23.44.020.E. NC1/NC2 size limits: SDCI Commercial Zoning Summary (October 2019).
_meta.rule_check_levels: Each rule in the rules section has a check_level: unchecked, transcribed or reviewed (see rules._note and docs/verifying-rules.md). All rules start unchecked. sections_read is the record of code sections read from seattle.gov's 2021 code PDFs; a rule can be transcribed only when every section it names is in that record and marked complete. The site, the PDFs and the assistant show each finding's level and how many rules are at each level. The level never changes a finding's status.

Exception 1: no exit signs where only one exit is required.
The business and mercantile rows were garbled in the text extract: re-read them before transcribing PL-1 or PL-2.
Ground-floor shops and restaurants up to 2,500 sq ft in Neighborhood Residential zones.

_meta.verify: Entered from memory and not checked against Seattle's text: the occupancy group for each business type, the occupant load factor used for waiting areas, the hood and extinguisher sections, the ADA section numbers, the state salon licence, and the zoning status of downtown, Seattle Mixed, multifamily and industrial zones and of bars and gyms in each zone. Also from memory: how many urinals may stand in for required toilets, 67% in assembly spaces and 50% in others (plumbing.urinal_substitution, SBC 2902.1.1); the 75 ft of travel to a fire extinguisher (fire.extinguisher_max_travel_ft), the 28 to 34 in. accessible table surface height (accessibility.table_surface_height_in) and the 5 to 7 months a land use approval can take (zoning.land_use_approval_time). Check each before relying on it.

rules._note: One entry per rule id the checker reports. check_level is unchecked, transcribed or reviewed (docs/verifying-rules.md). unchecked: nobody has yet compared every number and condition with the code text. transcribed: a person compared them with the 2021 Seattle Building Code text and recorded who (transcribed_by) and when (transcribed_on); every section the source names must be in _meta.sections_read. reviewed: an expert also reviewed it, recorded as reviewed_by (name and role), reviewed_on and an optional review_note. source is the code edition and section. A rule missing here counts as unchecked. depends_on names the rules whose results this one uses (the occupant load OL-0, the occupancy group OCC-1, the number of exits EG-1): a finding's level is the lowest level of its rule and every rule it depends on. The level never changes a finding's status.

zoning.residential_commercial_note: Residential-Commercial (RC) zones allow limited ground-floor commercial uses.

NC1.note: Neighborhood Commercial 1. Most uses are limited to 10,000 sq ft.

drinking_establishment.note: Bars and taverns need a conditional use approval here and are limited to 10,000 sq ft.

NC2.note: Neighborhood Commercial 2. Most uses are limited to 25,000 sq ft.

drinking_establishment.note: Bars and taverns need a conditional use approval here and are limited to 25,000 sq ft.

DMR.note: Downtown Mixed Residential; commercial use depends on the R or C suffix.

PSM.note: Pioneer Square Mixed, a preservation district. Changes need a Certificate of Approval from the Department of Neighborhoods.

IDM.note: International District Mixed, a special review district. Changes need a Certificate of Approval from the Department of Neighborhoods.

IDR.note: International District Residential, a special review district. Changes need a Certificate of Approval from the Department of Neighborhoods.

PMM.note: Pike Market Mixed; the Pike Place Market Historical Commission reviews uses and changes.

NR.note: Neighborhood Residential. Ground-floor restaurants and shops are allowed only up to 2,500 sq ft, on or below the ground floor, closed 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., with no drive-in and with exhaust vents at least 10 ft above the sidewalk.

LR1.note: Lowrise 1 multifamily. Commercial uses are generally allowed only where the zone has an RC suffix.

LR2.note: Lowrise 2 multifamily. Commercial uses are generally allowed only where the zone has an RC suffix.

LR3.note: Lowrise 3 multifamily. Commercial uses are generally allowed only where the zone has an RC suffix.

MR.note: Midrise multifamily. Ground-floor commercial uses are limited.

HR.note: Highrise multifamily. Ground-floor commercial uses are limited.

UX.note: Urban Industrial; non-industrial uses have size limits.

MML.note: Maritime Manufacturing and Logistics; non-industrial uses have tight size limits.

II.note: Industry and Innovation; non-industrial uses have size limits.

IC.note: Industrial Commercial; non-industrial uses have size limits.

IB.note: Industrial Buffer; non-industrial uses have size limits.

IG.note: General Industrial; non-industrial uses have size limits.

MIO.note: Major Institution Overlay; the underlying zone and the institution's master plan both apply.
